name: Sloths can hold their breath longer than dolphins

hook_variants.template: The slowest land animal out-swims dolphins at holding its breath.
Which animal holds its breath longer: a dolphin or a sloth?
A sloth can stay underwater for 40 minutes. A dolphin: about 10.

sections.text: Sloths can hold their breath for up to 40 minutes underwater. Typical dolphin dives: around 10 minutes.
Their heart rate drops to about a third of normal, letting them conserve oxygen.
sections.title: the trick

sections.text: They do this by slowing their heartbeat to a crawl — bradycardia on demand.
sections.title: mechanism

sections.text: Their resting heart rate is already only about 25 beats per minute.
sections.subtitle: one of the slowest of any mammal

sections.text: So while dolphins are faster in the water, sloths win the deep-breath contest.
Follow for more facts about the animal kingdom's dark horses.

facts.claim: Sloths can hold their breath underwater for up to 40 minutes by slowing their heart rate
Dolphins typically dive for about 10 minutes, with some species longer
A sloth's resting heart rate is around 25 beats per minute
